summary: Worst-case search must inspect the tree, and every value in every qualifying returned path must be written. Shared-buffer backtracking matches the resulting output-sensitive linear bound.

optimality.argument: Here n is the number of tree nodes and L is the total number of values across all returned paths. An absent-match instance can require inspection of all n nodes, while any instance with qualifying paths requires writing all L output values; complete equal-depth trees can realize both obligations together. Thus the worst-case lower bound is Omega(n + L). The current DFS performs constant traversal work per node and copies only qualifying paths, for O(n + L) time and O(h) auxiliary recursion and path space.

replacement_checks.evidence: All n nodes may need inspection, and the required result explicitly contains L values that must each be materialized.
Each node is entered and exited once, while path copying writes exactly the L values present in the final output.
The source-fidelity-verified examples cover multiple matches and two distinct no-match forms; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
